title: Keeping a Seed Library Useful
transcript:
The seed library at Oak Street Community Centre looks like a small set of drawers, but its organiser says the labels matter more than the furniture. I visited the centre to ask volunteer Ruth Lane how the scheme works. Residents take a small packet of seeds, grow the plants, and, if they can, bring back fresh seeds for other people to use. Returning seeds is encouraged, but it is not a condition of borrowing.

Ruth explained that the first collection included many packets marked only with the name of a vegetable. Some gardeners waited months for beans that were not suited to the local growing season. The library now asks donors to record when the seeds were collected and whether the parent plants were grown outdoors or under cover.

I wondered if the extra information discouraged donations. Ruth said the total number of packets had fallen slightly, but more of them were useful. Volunteers also keep a small trial bed behind the centre. If they are unsure about a donation, they plant a few seeds before offering the rest.

The scheme has attracted people who have never grown food before. Ruth advises them to start with one container and a crop they actually enjoy eating. She does not want beginners to spend money preparing a large garden, only to become discouraged. Next spring, the centre will hold short sessions on reading seed labels before it offers more advanced gardening workshops.

questions.prompt: What is expected of people who take seeds?
options: They must return twice as many seeds.
They must pay for every packet.
They must already own a garden.
They are encouraged, but not required, to return fresh seeds.
questions.answer: They are encouraged, but not required, to return fresh seeds.
questions.explanation: 归还新种子受到鼓励，但不是领取种子的前提。

questions.prompt: What problem occurred with some early donations?
options: The seeds were unsuitable for the local growing season.
The packets contained too many written instructions.
Donors asked volunteers to sell the vegetables.
The drawers were kept outside in the rain.
questions.answer: The seeds were unsuitable for the local growing season.
questions.explanation: 最初部分种子只标蔬菜名称，领到不适合当地生长季的豆类后，种植者等了很久仍无收获。

questions.prompt: Why do volunteers use the trial bed?
options: To grow all the centre's food.
To test uncertain donations before sharing the remaining seeds.
To compare the prices of gardening tools.
To teach visitors how to build wooden drawers.
questions.answer: To test uncertain donations before sharing the remaining seeds.
questions.explanation: 对不确定的捐赠种子，志愿者先试种一部分，再决定是否分发其余种子。

questions.prompt: What does Ruth recommend to beginners?
options: Choose a vegetable they have never tasted.
Start small with something they like eating.
Attend advanced workshops before planting anything.
questions.answer: Start small with something they like eating.
questions.explanation: 她建议初学者从一个容器和自己爱吃的作物开始，避免投入过大后受挫。
